sub_questions.q: Which models does the paper propose?
sub_questions.answer: The paper proposes GRURNTN and LSTMRNTN.
sub_questions.quote: Our proposed RNNs, which are called a Long-Short Term Memory Recurrent Neural Tensor Network (LSTMRNTN) and Gated Recurrent Unit Recurrent Neural Tensor Network (GRURNTN)

sub_questions.q: What word-level test perplexity does the paper report on Penn Treebank for each proposed model?
sub_questions.answer: The paper reports word-level PTB test perplexity 87.38 for GRURNTN and 96.97 for LSTMRNTN.
sub_questions.section: V-B Word-level Language Modeling, Table II

sub_questions.q: In what experimental setting are the proposed models' word-level Penn Treebank test perplexities reported?
sub_questions.answer: The proposed models are reported as individual models; the paper states that the baseline and proposed model experiments did not use dynamic evaluation. No cache/pointer, ensemble, or fine-tuning setting is reported for the proposed word-level results.
sub_questions.quote: Our baseline and proposed model experiment did not use dynamic evaluation.
sub_questions.section: V-A Character-level Language Modeling, Table I footnote

sub_questions.q: Which baseline models and published results does the paper list for word-level Penn Treebank test perplexity?
sub_questions.answer: The paper lists GRURNN (97.78) and LSTMRNN (108.26) as baselines, plus N-Gram (141), RNNLM without dynamic evaluation (124.7), RNNLM with dynamic evaluation (123.2), SCRNN (115), sRNN (110.0), and DOT(S)-RNN (107.5).
sub_questions.quote: GRURNN (our baseline) 97.78 LSTMRNN (our baseline) 108.26 N-Gram [24] 141 RNNLM (w/o dyn. eval) 124.7 RNNLM (w/ dyn. eval) 123.2 SCRNN [33] 115 sRNN [12] 110.0 DOT(S)-RNN [12] 107.5
sub_questions.section: V-B Word-level Language Modeling, Table II

sub_questions.q: How do the proposed models' word-level Penn Treebank test perplexities compare with the baseline models and other listed results?
sub_questions.answer: Both proposed models outperform their baselines. GRURNTN reduces PPL from 97.78 to 87.38 over GRURNN (10.4 absolute / 10.63% relative), and LSTMRNTN reduces PPL from 108.26 to 96.97 over LSTMRNN (11.29 absolute / 10.42% relative). GRURNTN outperforms all baselines and other listed models; LSTMRNTN closely resembles baseline GRURNN.
sub_questions.quote: Overall, LSTMRNTN improved the LSTMRNN model and its performance closely resembles the baseline GRURNN. However, GRURNTN outperformed all the baseline models as well as the other models by a large margin.
